content.thinking: I should swap "within about a minute" for something simpler like "quickly" or "in a short time," and double-check other number phrasing like "first" and "only" since those seem fine as is. Time to resubmit with that fix.

action_items.item: Require the io-shop test suite to pass with a feature flag switched on before that flag can be switched on in production.
Roll out io-shop feature flags in stages, holding at a small share of evaluations before going further.
Turn a flag rollout back automatically when the account page error rate rises while the rollout is in progress.

causal_chain.step: Account pages failed for some shoppers: the share of requests failing rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_at_worst} at its worst, and account page request failures were logged throughout.

The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in the monthly spend summary in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. This error first appears at the onset and is logged only while the incident lasted.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: none came back for the day before the onset, and the only production change read was this flag switch.
Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed only this change by anyone other than Argus in the hour before.

causal_chain.step: That code path ran because admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. Before that, every evaluation was off and account pages rendered normally. From {G971b.1} some evaluations were on, and soon after that all of them were. Argus turned the flag off and the service came back, and that action was judged confirmed.

With the flag on, the monthly path divides the month's spend by the number of purchases flagged as this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is {F1.1}. This comes from Code-Fix reading the source and is unverified: nothing ran its tests or its fix.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly-spending feature made the shop's account pages run a calculation that crashed by dividing by an empty count of purchases, likely for shoppers who had bought before but nothing this month.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that ran account pages with monthly-spend-feature on, for a shopper who had bought before but not this month, before the flag was switched on in production. Code-Fix's reading says the existing test helper calls such a shopper the ordinary case.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The crash in the monthly path would have been found before the flag reached production shoppers, so turning the flag on would not have broken account pages.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from all evaluations off to all on very quickly. No staged hold and no automatic revert on the account page error rate were seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Fewer shoppers would have hit the failing path before the error rate showed, and the flag could have been turned back sooner.

went_well: Argus turned monthly-spend-feature off {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The action was judged confirmed {T21.1 - T18.1} after the flag was turned off.
Reading the flag provider's history (T15) and the change events (T9) narrowed the trigger to this flag switch, with no deploy involved.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, account page requests go through the monthly spend summary in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, which raised ZeroDivisionError (G5309). Code-Fix read the source but nothing ran its reading. By that reading, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides the month's total by the number of purchases made this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is {F1.1}, and nothing in the code guards against it.
input.still_at_risk: The faulty monthly spend calculation is still in the code behind the flag, so switching monthly-spend-feature on again before a fix is in place would likely make account pages fail for the same shoppers again.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
